title: Approval channels
description: The approval service's delivery adapters (F1c B2, design D3; bin/approvals.py). One row per channel: deliver gets the request (no secret) as JSON on stdin and prints its message ref; collect gets the pending requests delivered on that channel as a JSON array on stdin ({id, nonce, message_ref}) and prints one JSON answer line per answer ({request_id, nonce, decision: approved|denied, user, message_ref, digest?}). A new channel, of a known kind or a new one, is a new row: no code change. Whether a kind may answer is the owner-auth policy's channel_kinds, never this file. An argv's first item is a path relative to the stack root (no .. part) or an absolute path. Owner-only: only the owner path writes it.

host_kind.description: The channel kind of the host terminal's own answer (approvals.py answer, proved by the owner key); whether it may answer is the owner-auth policy's channel_kinds.

adapter_timeout_s.description: How long one deliver or collect run may take; past it the adapter is killed and its run fails (STL-OWN-830).

ask_ttl_s.description: The ttl (seconds) of a request intake makes from an agent's approval-ask.

env.description: The fixed environment every deliver, collect and resume runs with (RT2-4: nothing else of the caller's environment is inherited, so a program planted in a folder on the caller's PATH, or BASH_ENV, never runs). path: PATH, in order, absolute folders only (no : in one; put folders agents can write last, so they never shadow a system tool). pass: the caller's variables passed by name when set (scratch roots, owner config file, Discord helper). A row's argv words that are variable names (an owner config key such as its channel id) pass for that argv too.

resume.description: Runs once per decision (an accepted answer approved or denied, or the expiry: expired), never while pending: argv plus the request's card id and the decision word, and the decision as JSON on stdin (board unblock).

kind.description: A free id, not a code enum: whether it answers is the owner-auth policy's channel_kinds (a kind not listed answers nothing).
